text: Smaller private funds spend more on compliance than larger ones, both as a share of AUM and relative to operating costs, which means increasing regulatory scrutiny falls disproportionately on smaller funds.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Post Dodd-Frank Act Evolution of the Private Fund Industry Comparative Evidence from 2012 and 2 (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2739479

isBasedOn.name: The Post Dodd-Frank Act Evolution of the Private Fund Industry Comparative Evidence from 2012 and 2

abstract: Smaller private funds spend more on compliance costs than their larger counterparts—both as a percentage of AUM and in relation to oper- ating costs; this suggests that increasing regulatory scrutiny disproportionately impacts smaller funds.

value: private fund advisers subject to Dodd-Frank compliance obligations
compliance measured as share of AUM and of operating costs
